title: Implement dual-signature update verification

addedDependencies.name: membrane-updater
addedDependencies.reason: Reuses this task's own pure admission crate (already an engine/Cargo.toml workspace member, already depended on by nothing else) from the Tauri app's adapter. No new external crate was added; membrane-updater itself gained no new dependency beyond its existing serde.workspace = true.

correctionApplied.summary: The orchestrator corrected the initial brief mid-task: do not hand-roll signing/notarization/updater-signature logic, since RightKit already owns and produces both signatures for this app. Before writing the adapter, this task read apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs, apps/membrane-hub/package.json's release:* scripts, and tools/rightkit/packages/release/{create-mac-updater,sign-updater,publish-update,notary-auth,runtime-artifact-manifest,asr-artifact-adoption,hardeningscan}.mjs.
correctionApplied.designChangeAsResult: No bespoke signing logic existed before this correction landed (the pre-existing scaffold at commit 5cddb0b7 was already pure/adapter-shaped and never signed anything itself, so nothing needed to be torn out). The correction instead shaped how the *new* adapter code in this task binds to real evidence: apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/src/update_admission.rs::RightKitUpdaterManifestEntry mirrors tools/rightkit/packages/release/publish-update.mjs's real `platforms[<target>] = { signature, url }` manifest shape field-for-field (the signature RightKit already produces via sign-updater.mjs against the shared rightsuite-updater-key), and ::PlatformAcceptanceReceipt mirrors scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs's orthic.membrane.platform-acceptance.v1 schema field-for-field. Neither struct invents a field RightKit/the existing receipt schema does not already have. scripts/release/updater/contract.mjs imports (not duplicates) verify-platform-artifacts.mjs's validateReceipt. No ed25519/signing crate was added to Cargo.toml; no codesign/spctl/signtool/notarytool invocation was written anywhere in this task's Rust or JS. tests/update/dual-signature.test.mjs gained an explicit assertion that the pure crate's source never references ed25519/ring/dalek/rsa/a raw Verifier::verify call, enforcing this as a standing contract, not just a one-time choice.

notes: This task builds on the prior scaffold at commit 5cddb0b7 ('feat(updater): add dual-trust update admission contract'), already on main, which added engine/crates/membrane-updater (Platform, TauriSignatureEvidence, PlatformTrustEvidence, UpdateCandidate, UpdateTrustVerifier trait, verify()), docs/update-dual-signature.md, and tests/update/dual-signature.test.mjs. That scaffold correctly kept the crate pure and adapter-based (no hand-rolled crypto) but had one real gap against this task's acceptance criterion: `verify()` never compared from_version/to_version numerically, so a downgrade to an older-but-validly-signed artifact would have passed identity_valid (which only required from != to) and gone on to the trust checks. This task closes that gap: FailureCode::DowngradeRejected, is_upgrade()/version_triple()/leading_digits(), checked before either trust domain runs (so a stale signed artifact is refused without ever asking a trusted adapter to look at it), plus 12 new #[test]s covering every fail-closed case the acceptance criterion names.

docs/update.md already existed as a different, MBR-204-owned document ('Transactional update': supervisor quiesce, staging, atomic activation, schema migration/rollback) -- unrelated to signatures. Per 'preserve unrelated user changes' this task appended a new '## Dual-signature verification (MBR-911)' section rather than overwriting the file, and explicitly notes that admission (this task) gates entry into that existing transactional flow but never performs it.

apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/src/update_admission.rs is written but not wired into the running tauri::Builder invoke handler (only `mod update_admission;` was added to main.rs). Reason: RightKit's own apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs declares an `updater` artifact block only for targets.win today, not targets.mac (matching packaging/macos/bundle-manifest.json's updater component, present:false, owned by the concurrent macOS release lane per MBR-901's evidence) -- there is no live end-to-end update flow yet to gate. This task ships the gate itself, fully tested against RightKit's real Windows shapes, ready to be called by whichever task wires the live tauri-plugin-updater flow; it does not invent that wiring or a mac RightKit config entry that does not exist yet, since packaging/macos/** and scripts/release/macos/** are outside this task's allowlist and owned by a concurrent lane.

scripts/release/updater/contract.mjs's UPDATER_PLATFORM_TO_RECEIPT_PLATFORM map registers only 'windows-x86_64' -> 'windows', matching exactly what right-release.config.mjs currently declares (targets.win.updater.artifacts[0].platform). A macOS entry is deliberately not guessed ahead of that config; a test (contract.test.mjs) pins this so the map cannot silently grow without an explicit review.

Two node --test files were actually executed for this task (see commands.log): tests/update/dual-signature.test.mjs (1 test, extended with downgrade + no-embedded-crypto assertions) and scripts/release/updater/contract.test.mjs (12 tests, new). All 13 pass. The Rust #[test] modules in engine/crates/membrane-updater/src/lib.rs (11 new tests) and apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/src/update_admission.rs (8 new tests) were reasoned through by type but not executed, per this task's hard rule against cargo test/check/build.

Credentials are referenced by name only where they appear at all (rightsuite-updater-key as a Keychain/env-var service name in doc comments, quoting RightKit's own existing scripts); no credential value was read, printed, exported, or copied anywhere in this task.
No mutating git command was run. This evidence bundle and the source files above are uncommitted; the orchestrator commits with the exact MBR-911 message.
